rationale.conceptual: The paper uses standard first-principles calculations (GGA-PBE, PAW) with special quasi-random structures and elastic constant extraction via strain methods. No novel algorithm is proposed; the challenge lies in the correct application of DFT convergence, k-point sampling, and post-processing (Voigt-Reuss-Hill averaging, DOS analysis), which requires familiarity with computational materials science but not deep novel research.
rationale.execution: The pipeline spans at least 9 stages: SQS generation with ATAT, DFT reference energies for elemental solids, full variable-cell relaxations, elastic constant calculations by applying strains, property derivation, and separate DOS and charge density evaluations for multiple alloys. Orchestration involves two external packages (ATAT, Quantum ESPRESSO), managing many I/O files, and ensuring consistency across runs; this is a long, fragile, multi-tool pipeline.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies standard DFT with SQS to compute structural and elastic properties of intermetallic alloys. The method is non-trivial but well-established; the reproduction requires a multi-stage pipeline with careful tool orchestration. Difficulty is moderate conceptually (3) but high in execution (4) due to many DFT runs and environment handling. Resources are modest CPU-based DFT calculations.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT calculations for 32-atom supercells with a 320 eV cutoff and 8x8x8 k-point mesh are CPU-only, requiring moderate memory (~4-8 GB per run). Input data (crystal structures) are tiny, and outputs (text-based energies, DOS) are a few MB in total.
